content: 1. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 2. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, as a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions from CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 3. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates, potentially leading to increased toxicity. 4. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used, as hormonal contraception alone is unreliable when taking lesinurad. 5. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Letrozole should not be administered concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 6. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels. 8. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 9. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, potentially affecting the absorption of oral medications. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 10. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 11. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce or continue lonafarnib at the starting dose. Monitor closely for arrhythmias and related events, as the effect of lonafarnib on the QT interval is unknown. 12. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring a higher growth hormone dose. 13. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 14. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects. 16. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Norelgestromin increases the levels of maraviroc by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is a potential for increased toxicity. 18. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may decrease systemic exposure to ethinylestradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during co-administration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 19. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Norelgestromin also decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. A subtherapeutic response to metyrapone may occur in patients on estrogen therapy, including oral contraceptives. Discontinuation of estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 22. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by altering hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 24. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norelgestromin and ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone also increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 26. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 28. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. 29. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 31. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ethinylestradiol increases the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 35. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of norelgestromin and ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, potentially increasing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for decreased systemic levels of sensitive CYP substrates after initiating nemolizumab. 36. Neomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 38. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. 41. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. 42. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Ethinylestradiol and nortriptyline interact through an unspecified mechanism. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects of TCAs. Monitor closely. 44. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by altering hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Omaveloxolone may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills, due to weak CYP3A4 induction. 47. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir significantly increase the risk of ALT elevations when co-administered with ethinylestradiol. Discontinue ethinylestradiol-containing medications before initiating this hepatitis C combination regimen. Restart ethinylestradiol-containing medications approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 48. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. 49. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 50. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Use caution and monitor closely.
